messages.text: 'use proactively' marking found — encourages autonomous delegation

writing.overall_comment: A solid, well-organized test-generation prompt with clear conventions, but it needs explicit hand-back/scope boundaries and a tighter output contract to be a fully reliable subagent definition.

dimensions.name: Delegation fit
dimensions.comment: The description names the trigger (Java unit tests with JUnit/Mockito/AssertJ) clearly enough for a main agent to route, but omits the Java 8/Gradle context and the exclusions (integration tests, non-test code) that would sharpen routing.

dimensions.name: Prompt quality
dimensions.comment: Role, mandatory naming convention, AAA structure, coverage strategy, and a five-step workflow are explicit, but the output contract is loose—no target path/package convention, no requirement to run or verify the generated tests.

dimensions.name: Boundaries
dimensions.comment: Style-level prohibitions are listed (no private-method tests, no POJO mocks), yet there is no scope boundary such as 'never modify production code' or a hand-back condition when the class under test or its dependencies are ambiguous.

dimensions.name: Conciseness
dimensions.comment: The prompt is short and well-sectioned with minimal filler, though the naming-convention example block and the external `~/.claude/docs/...` reference add a little dead weight.

suggestions: In the skill description or boundary instructions, add an explicit scope boundary that the skill must never modify production code and must hand back when the class under test or its dependencies are ambiguous.
In the skill description, add the missing Java 8/Gradle context so the main agent can accurately route JUnit/Mockito/AssertJ unit-test tasks.
In the skill description, add explicit exclusions for integration tests and non-test code to prevent misrouting.
